import pandas as pd


REQUIRED_COLUMNS = ("Created Date", "Close Date")


def parse_dates(df):
    # A frame with no columns means the source file was empty or not read.
    # Fail with a clear message instead of a misleading "missing columns" KeyError.
    if df.shape[1] == 0:
        raise ValueError("No columns to parse: the input file is empty or was not read.")

    # Promote the first row to the header only when the file was read without one
    # (default integer column labels) and there is at least one row to promote.
    if len(df) > 0 and all(isinstance(c, int) for c in df.columns):
        header = df.iloc[0]
        df = df.iloc[1:].copy()
        df.columns = [str(v) for v in header]
        df = df.reset_index(drop=True)

    # Normalize header names to remove stray whitespace and BOM characters.
    df.columns = [str(c).strip().lstrip("\ufeff") for c in df.columns]

    missing = [col for col in REQUIRED_COLUMNS if col not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing expected columns: {missing}. Found: {list(df.columns)}")

    df["Created Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Created Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")
    df["Close Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Close Date"], format="%Y-%m-%d")
    return df
